brief.why: A security audit flagged that a stolen refresh token stays valid until it expires.
brief.what: Rotate the refresh token on every use and revoke the whole token family when an old one is reused.
brief.impact: Every signed-in customer on the website and mobile apps; clients must store the new token after each refresh.

complexity.reason: Rotation with reuse detection, a migration on a hot table and a new background job.

worst_case.scenario: A bug in rotation or reuse detection logs every customer out, or silently weakens session security.

audience.reason: The refresh endpoint is called by the public website and mobile apps for every signed-in customer.

factors.description: Two tabs refreshing at once will both present the same token; the second is treated as reuse and revokes the family, logging the user out.
Adding a NOT NULL column with a default to `sessions` rewrites the table on older Postgres versions.
Families are pruned by creation date rather than last use, which may delete active long-lived sessions.

intent.stated_intent: Harden session security by rotating refresh tokens and detecting token reuse, as required by the security audit.
intent.inferred_intent: Implements rotation and family revocation, and also changes the session TTL from 30 to 14 days, which is not mentioned in the description.
intent.alignment: Mostly aligned. The TTL change is scope creep and has user-facing impact; it should be called out or split out.

decisions.decision: Revoke the entire token family on reuse
decisions.rationale: Follows the OAuth 2.0 Security BCP recommendation (quoted in the description).
decisions.alternatives: Revoke only the reused token; alert without revoking.

decisions.decision: Store token hashes instead of raw tokens
decisions.rationale: Inferred: limits damage if the sessions table leaks.

open_questions: How are concurrent refreshes from multiple tabs handled?
Was the TTL change from 30 to 14 days intentional?
Is there a rollout plan for already-issued tokens?

affected_components.name: Auth service
affected_components.description: Refresh endpoint behaviour changes; clients must store the new token on every refresh.

affected_components.name: Web & mobile clients
affected_components.description: Must replace the stored refresh token after each call.

breaking_changes: Clients that reuse the old refresh token will be logged out.
Session lifetime reduced from 30 to 14 days.
downstream_effects: Mobile app versions older than 5.2 do not persist rotated tokens.
data_and_migrations: New token_family column on sessions; backfill required.
security: Detects and contains stolen refresh tokens.
impact.test_coverage: Unit tests cover rotation and reuse, but there is no test for concurrent refreshes or for the migration.
suggested_tests: Two concurrent refreshes with the same token
Migration on a copy of production data

service_impact.reason: Refresh endpoint and token storage change in the public API.
Customer authentication relayed by Fibra now expects rotated tokens.
Must store the new refresh token after every call or users get logged out.
Product modal reads the catalogue with the same session.
PromoStandards credentials unaffected; listed for awareness.
